title: O Maidens in Your Savage Season
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Five girls in a high school literature club, written by Mari Okada, are thrown into confusion when classic novels and a club discussion turn their thoughts to sex. Kazusa struggles with feelings for childhood friend Izumi, Niina carries a past of grooming by an acting coach, Momoko realizes she is attracted to girls, club president Sonezaki wrestles with a strict upbringing, and writer Hitoha pursues a teacher she met in an adult chat room.
life_message: Growing up means facing desire and love honestly, telling attraction from affection, and keeping faith with friends through it.

content.note: Emotional melodrama; Niina's grooming history (Wikipedia) is unsettling.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts resolved through talk and friendship, not retaliation; mockery from popular classmates is endured.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Sonezaki's strict upbringing loosens; girls pursue their own desires.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Club friendships matter more than families in the summaries.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Hitoha blackmails a teacher; adult authority is weak.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Shame-based purity is questioned; feelings examined through literature.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Exploring identity and sexuality, including Momoko's queerness, is the core.

folkways.japan: School clubs, childhood-friend bonds and social pressure from popular classmates reflect Japanese school culture, as does the euphemistic way sex is first approached.

delivery.evidence: ANN calls it a frank discussion of female sexuality; characters debate sex openly. Reviews cover the anime.

personified.ideology: Shame-based purity from a strict upbringing
Seeking sexual experience as material for art

delivery.note: The prudish view is voiced by a sympathetic heroine who grows, while the story still leans toward openness about desire.

winners_losers: Sonezaki gains a healthy relationship by learning to separate affection from attraction; Momoko's love goes unrequited; openness about desire gets more sympathy than shame.
